title.en: It is how you know it is hers

can_do: I can describe what makes a writer's prose recognisable.
I can imitate another writer's grammar closely enough to show what it is.
I can hear my own habits in my own writing.

ex: An erudite footnote that quietly corrects the whole chapter.
He is erudite and he never makes you feel it.
The lecture drew every savant in the region and forty students.
Treating him as a savant let everyone avoid arguing with him.
The iconoclast of 1985 is the establishment of 2010.
Being an iconoclast is easy; being right afterwards is not.
The manual is written for the neophyte and read by everyone.
A neophyte's question exposed a hole nobody had noticed.
The pedagogue in him takes over about ten minutes into any dinner.
He was a great pedagogue and an impossible colleague.
The new supervisor is a martinet about the sign-in sheet.
A martinet keeps the trains running and empties the office.
Calling your opponents philistines is not an argument.
He plays the philistine and has read more than any of us.
The reform needed believers and attracted zealots.
A zealot on the committee costs you every compromise.
A doctrinaire reading of the rule would close the school.
She is principled without being doctrinaire, which is rarer than it sounds.
A hidebound department that has used the same form since 1978.
Hidebound is not the same as careful, though it often claims to be.
Her taste in music is catholic and her taste in tea is not.
The library's holdings are catholic to the point of disorder.
An eclectic method that borrows whatever works.
The programme is eclectic and the running order makes no sense.
A mercurial editor: two pages of praise, then silence for a month.
Mercurial in negotiation, and perfectly steady once he signs.
The market stayed volatile for six weeks after the announcement.
A volatile meeting that could have gone either way.
An equable man who has never once raised his voice in a meeting.
The climate there is equable, which is the whole reason for the orchards.
He was phlegmatic about the loss and back at work on Monday.
A phlegmatic response to news that emptied the room.
A placid child who watched everything and said little.
The lake is placid at six and unusable by nine.
She was stoic about the diagnosis and furious about the waiting list.
Stoic silence is not always strength; sometimes it is just silence.
A stolid defence that gave nothing away for ninety minutes.
His stolid expression told the room absolutely nothing.
A staid institution that has just hired its first designer.
The staid cover hides a very strange book.
A dour man who turned out to be the kindest on the floor.
The dour mood of the meeting lifted when the figures arrived.
He went morose for a week and then told us what had happened.
Morose at breakfast, unrecognisable by the afternoon.
A lugubrious speech at a party that was going perfectly well.
His lugubrious face is a joke he has been making for thirty years.

grammar.label: voice — the sound of one writer and not another
grammar.form: characteristic sentence length, lexical range, punctuation habits and stance
grammar.meaning: makes prose recognisable as a particular person's

explanation.en: Voice is not a device; it is the accumulated residue of a thousand small choices, and it is visible in exactly those choices. A writer who always uses the semicolon, always concedes before arguing, always ends on the short clause has a voice whether or not she intended one. At C2 you can hear another writer's and, more usefully, hear your own.
explanation.uz: Ovoz — vosita emas, mingta kichik tanlovning yig'indisi. C2 darajada boshqa yozuvchining ovozini eshitish va, muhimrog'i, o'zingnikini eshitish mumkin.

grammar.positive_example: She concedes in the first sentence of every paragraph; it is how you know it is hers.
grammar.negative_example: She has a very strong voice, which means that her writing is generally good.

l1_notes.uz: Individual yozuv ovozi tushunchasi ingliz adabiy tanqidida markaziy; uni o'lchab bo'lmaydi, lekin ko'rsatish mumkin.

grammar.label: pastiche and parody — writing in someone else's grammar
grammar.form: reproducing another writer's syntax, lexis and stance, straight or exaggerated
grammar.meaning: imitates a voice, in tribute or in mockery

explanation.en: To parody a writer you must first analyse them, which is why parody is the sharpest form of criticism: it demonstrates the mannerism rather than describing it. Pastiche imitates without mockery; parody exaggerates the one feature that was always slightly too much. Both require you to hear the original exactly.
explanation.uz: Parodiya qilish uchun avval tahlil qilish kerak; shuning uchun parodiya — eng o'tkir tanqid shakli: u odatni tasvirlamaydi, ko'rsatadi.

grammar.positive_example: The parody works because it repeats the one habit he never noticed in himself.
grammar.negative_example: The parody works because it uses long words and sounds a bit like him.

l1_notes.uz: Parodiya asl matnni juda aniq eshitishni talab qiladi; bu C2 darajaning o'zi bir sinovi.

story.title: It is how you know it is hers

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Read those two paragraphs and tell me which one is Karimova.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: The second. The verbs are all in the same place and there is no adjective in front of a noun anywhere.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: That is her voice, and it was a habit long before it was a choice.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: I tried to write like her last month.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: I read it. It was a good imitation for a page and then it became a bad one.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Where you began to enjoy it. Pastiche is fair to the writer only while you are still working; after that it turns into parody whether you meant it or not.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: So the difference is the intention.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: The difference is the reader's judgement of the intention, which is not the same thing and is all you are ever given.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: You have one. You use a colon where other people use a dash, and you end every paragraph on the shortest sentence you can find.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Nobody knows their own. Somebody tells you, and then you can choose to keep it.
